stance.line: Several scheduling apps raised monthly plans this autumn. Owners told Hale some had less than a month's notice and no explanation of what they were paying for.
Podcast host Morgan Hale said vendors 'owe owners a straight answer, not a status page' after reminder texts stopped for several hours on Tuesday.
Reminders help at the margin. A fair deposit and a clear cancellation fee do more, and software firms oversell what a text can do.

interviewer_profile.read: Sympathetic to owners and sceptical of software vendors: presses on price rises, outages and data, and thinks reminders are oversold next to deposits.

goal: Owners leave believing no-shows are fixable this month, and visit our no-show guide.

messages.text: Most no-shows are preventable: a timely reminder and a fair deposit keep the calendar full.
Automatic reminders hand owners back the hours they spent on confirmation calls.
Owners deserve booking software that is honest about price and safe with client data.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: vid02 subtitles: the host opens every founder interview with the problem the guest set out to fix (2026-10-15)
questions_and_answers.question: What problem were you trying to fix when you started the company?
questions_and_answers.answer: No-shows. My co-founder ran a physio clinic and lost a day's takings most weeks to empty slots. Most no-shows are preventable: a timely reminder and a fair deposit keep the calendar full. Businesses in our September survey saw 56% fewer no-shows after 90 days with reminders, and that's the problem we still work on every day.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Our no-show guide and survey results, published 2026-10-20
questions_and_answers.question: You've just published a no-show survey. What did it find?
questions_and_answers.answer: It found no-shows can be cut fast. Businesses in our September survey saw 56% fewer no-shows after 90 days with reminders, and owners who also take a deposit had a median no-show rate of 3%. That's 412 owners answering, so it's their experience, not a lab test. A reminder at the right time plus a fair deposit keeps the calendar full.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: It found no-shows can be cut fast.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Regular topic 'no-shows': 4 of 12 recent pieces, latest vid03 (2026-10-08)
questions_and_answers.question: What does a no-show really cost a small salon or clinic?
questions_and_answers.answer: More than most owners think: the slot, the staff time, the client who'd have taken it, and the hours spent phoning clients to confirm. Owners in our September survey cut time spent confirming appointments by phone from 4 hours a week to 1, after 90 days with reminders. Automatic reminders hand owners back the hours they spent on confirmation calls.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: More than most owners think: the slot, the staff time, the client who'd have taken it, and the hours spent phoning clients to confirm.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Regular topic 'deposits and cancellation fees': 3 recent pieces; Hale's blog of 2026-08-12 says no-shows are a pricing problem
questions_and_answers.question: You've argued no-shows are a pricing problem, not a reminder problem. Aren't you overselling reminders?
questions_and_answers.answer: Reminders alone won't fix every no-show, and you're right that price matters. In our September survey, owners who also take a deposit for long or first appointments had a median no-show rate of 3%, against 7% for those who don't. Put the two together and most no-shows are preventable.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: Reminders alone won't fix every no-show, and you're right that price matters.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Regular topic 'pricing and price rises': 3 recent pieces, including vid04 (2026-10-01) and the 2026-10-20 article
questions_and_answers.question: Why do software subscriptions keep creeping up for small businesses?
questions_and_answers.answer: Text messages cost more to send this year, and that's real. But owners deserve booking software that is honest about price. When we changed ours, we gave 33 days' notice and existing customers keep the old price until January 1. Every vendor should explain what changed and give owners time.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: Text messages cost more to send this year, and that's real.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Regular topic 'software reliability and client data': 5 recent pieces, including vid02 (2026-10-15) and Hale's data checklist (2026-10-06)
questions_and_answers.question: What happens to a client's phone number after the reminder goes out?
questions_and_answers.answer: It stays with that business, for that business's reminders. Client phone numbers are used only for that business's reminders and are never sold, and the owner can export or delete them at any time. Owners deserve booking software that is honest about price and safe with client data, and that starts with a clear policy.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: It stays with that business, for that business's reminders.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: vid02 subtitles: the host asked 'half of what, and who measured it?' of a survey figure (2026-10-15)
questions_and_answers.question: You say reminders cut no-shows by 56%. Who measured that?
questions_and_answers.answer: Our customers did, in a survey we ran in September. 412 businesses answered, and the median no-show rate fell from 12.5% to 5.5% after 90 days: 56% fewer no-shows. It's self-reported and it's the owners who replied, not everyone, so I'd call it a strong signal rather than a lab result.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: Our customers did, in a survey we ran in September.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Backup figure P7 (GA4, 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), the pasted talking point 'we're growing fast', and no customer count among the figures cleared to say
questions_and_answers.question: You say you're growing fast. How many paying customers do you have?
questions_and_answers.answer: That's not a number I've cleared to share today, so I won't guess at it. What I can give you is a dated figure: our website had 35% more visits in the six months to September than in the six months before. That's visits, not customers, and I'd rather be precise than give you a number I can't back up.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: That's not a number I've cleared to share today, so I won't guess at it.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Backup figure P8 (GA4, 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30): a figure still marked 'check before saying' invites a numbers question

questions_and_answers.answer: It's not only a US story. People in 11 countries visited our site in the 12 months to September, mostly from the US, the UK and Canada. That's visitors, not customers, so I won't stretch it. What I can prove is the fix: businesses in our September survey saw 56% fewer no-shows after 90 days with reminders.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: It's not only a US story.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: vid02 subtitles: 'Why should an owner pick you over the app they already pay for?' (2026-10-15)
questions_and_answers.question: Why should an owner switch from the app they already pay for?
questions_and_answers.answer: Maybe they shouldn't, if it already keeps their calendar full. The test is simple: count last month's no-shows and what they cost. If that number hurts, try reminders and a fair deposit. Businesses in our September survey saw 56% fewer no-shows after 90 days with reminders.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: Maybe they shouldn't, if it already keeps their calendar full.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Sore point: a rival says deposits drive clients away
questions_and_answers.question: Some of your rivals say deposits drive clients away. Are they wrong?
questions_and_answers.answer: For some businesses a deposit is the wrong call, and no owner should be pushed into one. For long or first appointments it helps when it's fair and explained up front: in our September survey, owners who take a deposit had a median no-show rate of 3%, against 7% for those who don't.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: For some businesses a deposit is the wrong call, and no owner should be pushed into one.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Sore point: Growth plan from $39 to $49 on 2026-10-01; Hale's article of 2026-10-20 on vendor price rises

questions_and_answers.answer: Yes, the Growth plan went from $39 to $49 a month on October 1, and I understand why owners notice that. We gave 33 days' notice, and existing customers keep the old price until January 1. Owners deserve booking software that is honest about price, and that's how we tried to do it.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: Yes, the Growth plan went from $39 to $49 a month on October 1, and I understand why owners notice that.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: Sore point: reminder delay on 2026-09-16; Hale was quoted on reminder failures on 2026-09-18
questions_and_answers.question: You had an outage in September. How many appointments got no reminder?

We posted an update every 30 minutes and every affected account got a month's credit. That's the straight answer owners deserve, and it's why we publish what happened, not just a status page.
questions_and_answers.first_sentence: None were lost, but more than 2,900 reminders went out late on September 16, for 3 hours 40 minutes.

questions_and_answers.why_likely: vid02 subtitles: two follow-ups after the outage question, including 'did anyone get a refund?' (2026-10-15)

questions_and_answers.first_sentence: Every affected account got a month's credit, applied automatically, so nobody had to ask for it.

scored_answers.question: You raised your Growth plan by 25% last month. Isn't that exactly what owners are angry about?
scored_answers.practice_answer: Look, every business has costs going up, and text messages in particular got more expensive this year, which nobody talks about, and to be honest we held our price for three years while everyone else moved. So I think if you look at the whole picture, and what owners get for the money, the Growth plan is still very good value compared with most apps out there, and we added a lot of features this year too, like waitlists and better calendar sync, so it really isn't the price hike people make it out to be. And honestly, when you add up what a single no-show costs a salon, the difference between the old plan and the new one is paid back the first time a reminder saves a slot, which happens most weeks for most of the owners we talk to.
unchecked_claims: we held our price for three years
we added a lot of features this year too, like waitlists and better calendar sync
scored_answers.feedback: The first sentence never says the price went up, so it sounds like a dodge, and at 142 words it runs past the podcast target. Two claims aren't in your brief or the ledger: 'we held our price for three years' and the new features (waitlists, calendar sync). Confirm each with a date and a source before the interview, or drop it. Open with the fact ($39 to $49 on October 1), give the notice and the protection for existing customers, drop 'to be honest' and 'price hike', and stop.
scored_answers.tighter_version: Yes, the Growth plan went from $39 to $49 a month on October 1, and I understand why owners notice that. We gave 33 days' notice, and existing customers keep the old price until January 1. Owners deserve booking software that is honest about price, and that's how we tried to do it.

scored_answers.question: You had an outage in September. How many appointments got no reminder?
scored_answers.practice_answer: None were lost: more than 2,900 reminders went out late on September 16, for 3 hours 40 minutes. Every affected account got a month's credit, and we posted an update every 30 minutes. Owners deserve a straight answer, so we publish what happened.
scored_answers.feedback: Answer first, fact, remedy, message, stop. Keep this one exactly as it is.

scored_answers.question: You say reminders cut no-shows by 56%. Who measured that?
scored_answers.practice_answer: Our customers measured it in a September survey of 412 businesses: 56% fewer no-shows after 90 days. It's self-reported, so it's a strong signal, not a lab result.
scored_answers.feedback: Good: who measured it, the sample size and the honest limit. It's short for a podcast; add the before and after rates (12.5% to 5.5%) to reach the target length.
scored_answers.tighter_version: Our customers did, in a survey we ran in September. 412 businesses answered, and the median no-show rate fell from 12.5% to 5.5% after 90 days: 56% fewer no-shows. It's self-reported and it's the owners who replied, not everyone, so I'd call it a strong signal rather than a lab result.

scored_answers.question: But who else can see those numbers? Your staff? Your text message provider?
scored_answers.practice_answer: Great question. We take security really seriously and we use industry-standard encryption everywhere, and our team is always thinking about how to protect owners and their clients, because trust is everything for a small business.
scored_answers.feedback: 'Great question' buys time but answers nothing, and 'industry-standard encryption' isn't what was asked. It also isn't in your data policy, so don't say it unless someone who knows the systems confirms it. Say who can see the numbers in the first sentence, then the never-sold line.
scored_answers.tighter_version: Only the people who need to send the reminder. Our text provider passes the message on and keeps nothing for its own use, and our support staff see a number only when an owner asks for help. Client phone numbers are used only for that business's reminders and are never sold.

scored_answers.question: Why should an owner switch from the app they already pay for?
scored_answers.practice_answer: Maybe they shouldn't switch, if their calendar is already full. Count last month's no-shows first and put a cost on them. If that number hurts, try reminders and a fair deposit; businesses in our September survey saw 56% fewer no-shows after 90 days.
scored_answers.feedback: Strong and generous: answers first, gives a test the owner can run, and lands the survey figure. Keep it.

scored_answers.question: Are you raising money to compete with the bigger apps?
scored_answers.practice_answer: There's nothing to announce on that. Our attention is on owners losing a day's takings to empty slots, because most no-shows are preventable with a timely reminder.
scored_answers.feedback: Right instinct on the off-limits topic, and it reaches a message. It's too short to sound comfortable and has no proof point: add a proof point, as the prepared answer does.
scored_answers.tighter_version: There's nothing to announce on that, and I won't speculate on air. Where our attention goes is easy to show: we sent more than 3.1 million reminders in the 12 months to September, because automatic reminders hand owners back the hours they spent on confirmation calls.
